title: Preparing a Club Newsletter

source.rights: 原创 AI 辅助虚构教学材料，尚待发布前独立审核。

questions.prompt: What number does the headline give for attendance?
questions.evidence: Leo: Good. The headline says fifty people attended the meeting. Does the source support that number?
questions.explanation: 标题写五十人；活动记录写二十。

questions.prompt: What number is in the attendance record?
questions.evidence: Maya: No. The attendance record says twenty. I will compare it with the organizer's notes before changing the text. The first paragraph currently repeats the larger number.

questions.prompt: Which day does the record give for the meeting?
questions.evidence: Leo: The picture caption also needs a change. It says the group met on Tuesday, but the record shows Thursday. Can you use the link to open the original note?
questions.explanation: 图片说明写周二，但记录显示周四。

questions.prompt: Why should the advertisement be labeled?
options: So the club can avoid checking the date.
So the interview can be deleted.
So readers do not confuse it with an article fact.
answers: So readers do not confuse it with an article fact.
questions.evidence: Leo: There is an advertisement below the picture. The publisher should label it clearly, so readers do not mistake it for a fact in the article.
questions.explanation: 清楚标记广告可以避免被当成正文事实。

questions.evidence: Maya: Agreed. The publication includes a quote from the club leader, and the citation points to our interview. I will check that we have copied her exact words.
questions.explanation: 引文出处指向他们的采访。

questions.prompt: What does the club require before sharing a recognizable photograph?
options: Permission from everyone who can be recognized.
answers: Permission from everyone who can be recognized.
questions.evidence: Leo: Before you forward the photograph, remember privacy. Our club rule says we must have permission from everyone who can be recognized. We do not have to print any names if people prefer not to be named.
questions.explanation: 此虚构俱乐部规则要求取得照片中可辨认者的许可。

questions.prompt: What alternative picture might they use?
options: A picture of the empty room.
A picture from a different event without checking.
A picture of the organizer’s password.
answers: A picture of the empty room.
questions.evidence: Maya: I will ask first. We might use a picture of the empty room if one person does not want to appear. May I add a comment asking readers for suggestions?
questions.explanation: 如果有人不愿出镜，可以考虑空房间的照片。

questions.prompt: What can the small icon open?
questions.evidence: Leo: Yes. Put it near the small icon that opens comments, and offer a way to subscribe to the newsletter. People should be able to find the contact details without opening an advertisement.

questions.prompt: Why is the claim that everyone loved the event uncertain?
options: Only six people gave an opinion.
answers: Only six people gave an opinion.
questions.evidence: Maya: One last point: the article says everyone loved the event. That claim may show bias because only six people gave an opinion.
questions.explanation: 只有六人表达意见，不能推断每个人都喜欢。

questions.prompt: When will Maya send the revised draft?
questions.evidence: Maya: I will send the revised draft this afternoon.
questions.explanation: Maya 说今天下午发送修改稿。

instructions: This conversation is fictional. Listen to the conversation before reading the transcript and answer independently. After submitting, check the transcript and reasons for any errors.
transcript:
Maya: I have finished the article about the library club, but I want to verify a few details before we publish it.
Leo: Good. The headline says fifty people attended the meeting. Does the source support that number?
Maya: No. The attendance record says twenty. I will compare it with the organizer's notes before changing the text. The first paragraph currently repeats the larger number.
Leo: The picture caption also needs a change. It says the group met on Tuesday, but the record shows Thursday. Can you use the link to open the original note?
Maya: Yes. The passage about the event mentions Thursday as well. I can zoom in on the image and enlarge the note, although that alone does not prove the date.
Leo: There is an advertisement below the picture. The publisher should label it clearly, so readers do not mistake it for a fact in the article.
Maya: Agreed. The publication includes a quote from the club leader, and the citation points to our interview. I will check that we have copied her exact words.
Leo: Before you forward the photograph, remember privacy. Our club rule says we must have permission from everyone who can be recognized. We do not have to print any names if people prefer not to be named.
Maya: I will ask first. We might use a picture of the empty room if one person does not want to appear. May I add a comment asking readers for suggestions?
Leo: Yes. Put it near the small icon that opens comments, and offer a way to subscribe to the newsletter. People should be able to find the contact details without opening an advertisement.
Maya: One last point: the article says everyone loved the event. That claim may show bias because only six people gave an opinion.
Leo: Then let's describe that limit. The result will be more useful if readers can see the evidence. We can print copies after the group approves the final version.
Maya: I will send the revised draft this afternoon.
